subject: general
question: Suresh spends 30% of his income on petrol, (1)/(4) of the remaining income on house rent, and the balance on food. If he spends ₹300 on petrol, then what is his expenditure on house rent?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expenditure on **petrol** = 30% of **Income** = ₹300.

⇒ 100% **Income** = (300 ÷ 30) × 100 = ₹1,000.

**Remaining income** after petrol = ₹1,000 − ₹300 = ₹700.

**House rent** = 1/4 of **Remaining income** = 700 ÷ 4 = ₹175.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d77e5a7cb957510554f0c0fd7ec86b3cfc2aae7e02344ec16404443a00214341.png] 

**Given:**

Expenditure on **petrol** = 30% of total income

Value of **petrol** expenditure = ₹300

**House rent** = 1/4 of **Remaining income**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total **income** be 'X'.

⇒ 30% of X = 300

⇒ (30/100) × X = 300

⇒ X = (300 × 100) ÷ 30 = ₹1,000

⇒ **Remaining income** = Total Income − Petrol expense

⇒ **Remaining income** = 1000 − 300 = ₹700

⇒ **House rent** = (1/4) × 700

⇒ **House rent** = ₹175

**∴ The correct answer is ₹175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When spending from a **remaining** amount, use the multiplying factor: Final = Initial × (1 − r₁) × (1 − r₂).

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

A fraction of 1/4 is equivalent to 25%. Calculating 1/4 of a value is the same as taking 25% of it.

Base Value Identification

Always identify if a percentage is applied to the **total income** or the **remaining income** to avoid calculation errors.
